title: Formulating simultaneous equations from problems
summary: Define variables, translate two independent conditions into linear equations and interpret the simultaneous solution in context.
objectives: Translate two independent totals or relationships into linear equations.
Solve, check and interpret the values in the original situation.

blocks.text: State what each variable represents, including units where relevant. Two unknowns require two independent conditions. Common models include total number, total cost, total mass, perimeter, age relationships and digit values.

sections.title: Translate one condition at a time

blocks.text: Words such as altogether usually signal addition, while “three more than” describes a difference. A cost or mass total is a weighted sum: quantity multiplied by value per item. Keep the two conditions separate until both equations are complete.

After solving, substitute into both model equations and read the question again. Counts must normally be whole and non-negative; digits lie from 0 to 9 and a tens digit cannot be zero. A mathematically valid intersection may still be unsuitable for the stated context.

prompt.text: Adult tickets cost S$8 and student tickets S$5. Twelve tickets earn S$75. Find each number.

content.text: Let x and y be adult and student ticket counts.

prompt.text: A two-digit number has digit sum 11 and is 27 greater than its reversal. Find it.

content.text: Let x be the tens digit and y the units digit.
Then x-y=3, so x=7 and y=4; the number is 74.

prompt.text: Two counts total 10 and differ by 4. Find the larger count.

feedback.text: The equations x+y=10 and x-y=4 give 2x=14, so x=7.

blocks.text: Name the mathematical relationship, choose a method that preserves it, and show each transformation clearly.
Check the result in every original condition and interpret endpoints, coordinates, roots or quantities in the form requested.
